problem_text: Two point charges of +3 μC and +6 μC are separated by 30 cm. What is the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them? (Use k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)

hints.text: What is the formula for the electrostatic force between two point charges?
Convert all units: μC to C, cm to m.
F = kq₁q₂/r²

problem_text: A point charge of +4 nC creates an electric field. What is the magnitude of the electric field at a distance of 2 m from the charge? (Use k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)

hints.text: What is the formula for the electric field from a point charge?
E = kq/r²
Convert nC to C: 1 nC = 10⁻⁹ C.

solution_explanation: Electric field from a point charge: E = kq/r² = (9×10⁹)(4×10⁻⁹)/(2)² = 36/4 = 9 N/C.

problem_text: Two charges, +2 μC at x = 0 and -2 μC at x = 4 m, are placed on the x-axis. What is the net electric field at x = 2 m? (Use k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)

hints.text: Calculate the electric field from each charge at x = 2 m.
Determine the direction of each field at the point of interest.
Both fields point in the +x direction (away from + charge, toward - charge).

solution_explanation: E from +2μC: E₁ = kq/r² = (9×10⁹)(2×10⁻⁶)/(2)² = 4500 N/C in +x direction. E from -2μC: E₂ = kq/r² = (9×10⁹)(2×10⁻⁶)/(2)² = 4500 N/C in +x direction (toward negative charge). Total: E = 4500 + 4500 = 9000 N/C. Wait, let me recalculate... Actually, the point is equidistant from both charges. E₁ points away from + charge (in +x), E₂ points toward - charge (also in +x). E_total = 2 × 9000 = 18000 N/C in +x direction.

problem_text: A uniform electric field E = 500 N/C exists between two large parallel plates. What is the electric flux through a rectangular area of 0.02 m² oriented perpendicular to the field?

hints.text: What is the formula for electric flux?
Φ = E · A = EA cos θ, where θ is the angle between E and the area normal.
For perpendicular orientation, θ = 0°, so cos θ = 1.

solution_explanation: Electric flux Φ = EA cos θ = (500)(0.02)(1) = 10 N·m²/C (or 10 V·m).

problem_text: A charge of +5 μC is moved from a point where the electric potential is 100 V to a point where it is 300 V. What is the change in potential energy of the charge?

pattern_refs.application_notes: Potential energy change from potential difference

hints.text: How is potential energy related to electric potential?
ΔU = qΔV
ΔV = V_final - V_initial = 300 - 100 = 200 V

solution_explanation: Change in potential energy: ΔU = qΔV = (5×10⁻⁶)(300-100) = (5×10⁻⁶)(200) = 1×10⁻³ J = 0.001 J = 1 mJ.

problem_text: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.01 m² separated by 0.001 m. What is its capacitance? (Use ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m)

hints.text: What is the formula for parallel-plate capacitance?
C = ε₀A/d
Make sure to use consistent units.

problem_text: A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows through the resistor?

hints.text: What is Ohm's law?
V = IR, so I = V/R

solution_explanation: Using Ohm's law: I = V/R = 12/4 = 3 A.

problem_text: In a circuit, three resistors (R₁ = 2Ω, R₂ = 3Ω, R₃ = 6Ω) are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

hints.text: For parallel resistors, what is the formula for equivalent resistance?
1/R_eq = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃
Find a common denominator or add the fractions.

solution_explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R_eq = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 2/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 1. So R_eq = 1 Ω.

problem_text: In the circuit shown, a 24 V battery is connected to two resistors: R₁ = 4Ω and R₂ = 8Ω in series. What is the current through the circuit?

hints.text: What is the total resistance in a series circuit?
R_total = R₁ + R₂ for series connection.
Then apply Ohm's law: I = V/R_total.

solution_explanation: Total resistance R_total = R₁ + R₂ = 4 + 8 = 12 Ω. Current I = V/R_total = 24/12 = 2 A.

problem_text: An electron (q = -1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C, m = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg) enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to its velocity of 2×10⁶ m/s. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on the electron?

hints.text: What is the formula for magnetic force on a moving charge?
F = qvB sin θ, where θ is the angle between v and B.
Since v is perpendicular to B, sin θ = 1.

solution_explanation: Magnetic force F = |q|vB sin θ = (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)(2×10⁶)(0.5)(1) = 1.6×10⁻¹³ N.

problem_text: A proton moves in a circular path of radius 0.2 m in a magnetic field of 0.1 T. What is the speed of the proton? (m_p = 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg, q = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)

hints.text: What force keeps the proton in circular motion?
Set magnetic force equal to centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r.
Solve for v: v = qBr/m.

solution_explanation: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: qvB = mv²/r. Solving for v: v = qBr/m = (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)(0.1)(0.2)/(1.67×10⁻²⁷) = 3.2×10⁻²¹/1.67×10⁻²⁷ = 1.92×10⁶ m/s.

problem_text: A straight wire carrying a current of 5 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.3 T. If 0.4 m of the wire is in the field and oriented perpendicular to it, what is the magnitude of the force on the wire?

hints.text: What is the formula for force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
F = BIL sin θ
Since the wire is perpendicular to B, sin θ = 1.

solution_explanation: Force on wire: F = BIL sin θ = (0.3)(5)(0.4)(1) = 0.6 N.

problem_text: A long straight wire carries a current of 10 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance of 0.05 m from the wire? (Use μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ T·m/A)

pattern_refs.application_notes: Magnetic field from long straight wire

hints.text: What is the formula for the magnetic field around a long straight wire?
B = μ₀I/(2πr)
This is a result from applying the Biot-Savart law or Ampere's law.

solution_explanation: Magnetic field from long wire: B = μ₀I/(2πr) = (4π×10⁻⁷)(10)/(2π×0.05) = (4×10⁻⁶)/(0.1) = 4×10⁻⁵ T = 40 μT.

problem_text: A circular loop of wire has 50 turns and radius 0.1 m. If the magnetic field through the loop changes from 0.2 T to 0.8 T in 0.02 s, what is the magnitude of the induced EMF?

hints.text: What is Faraday's law of induction?
EMF = -N × dΦ/dt = -N × A × dB/dt
Calculate the area A = πr² first.

problem_text: An inductor with inductance L = 0.5 H carries a current that changes at a rate of 4 A/s. What is the magnitude of the induced EMF across the inductor?

hints.text: What is the relationship between inductance and induced EMF?
EMF = -L × dI/dt
The magnitude is L × |dI/dt|.

solution_explanation: Induced EMF in inductor: |EMF| = L × |dI/dt| = 0.5 × 4 = 2 V.

problem_text: Two capacitors, C₁ = 3 μF and C₂ = 6 μF, are connected in series to a 12 V battery. What is the charge on each capacitor?

hints.text: For capacitors in series, what is the equivalent capacitance?
1/C_eq = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂
In series, each capacitor has the same charge: Q = C_eq × V.

solution_explanation: Equivalent capacitance: 1/C_eq = 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so C_eq = 2 μF. Charge: Q = C_eq × V = 2 × 12 = 24 μC. In series, both capacitors have the same charge.

problem_text: A junction in a circuit has three wires connected to it. If currents of 3 A and 5 A flow into the junction, what current must flow out?

hints.text: What does Kirchhoff's current law state?
Sum of currents into a junction = sum of currents out.
Conservation of charge requires I_in = I_out.

solution_explanation: By Kirchhoff's current law: currents in = currents out. 3 A + 5 A = I_out. So I_out = 8 A.

problem_text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V. What is its final kinetic energy in electron-volts (eV)?

pattern_refs.application_notes: Work done by electric field on charge

hints.text: How much work is done on a charge moving through a potential difference?
W = qΔV, and this work becomes kinetic energy.
1 eV is the energy an electron gains through 1 V potential difference.

solution_explanation: Work done = qΔV = (1e)(100 V) = 100 eV. This equals the final kinetic energy since the electron started from rest.

problem_text: A rectangular loop of wire (0.2 m × 0.1 m) is rotated in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the maximum magnetic flux through the loop?

hints.text: What is the formula for magnetic flux?
Φ = BA cos θ, where θ is the angle between B and the area normal.
Maximum flux occurs when the loop is perpendicular to B (θ = 0°).

solution_explanation: Area A = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 m². Maximum flux occurs when cos θ = 1: Φ_max = BA = (0.5)(0.02) = 0.01 Wb.

problem_text: A solenoid has 1000 turns, length 0.5 m, and radius 0.02 m. What is its inductance? (Use μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ H/m)

hints.text: What is the formula for the inductance of a solenoid?
L = μ₀n²Al = μ₀N²A/l, where n = N/l is turns per unit length.
Calculate cross-sectional area A = πr².
